title: Impact of temperature and diet on feeding and growth of a marine heterotrophic nanoflagellate
content:
ABSTRACT
Marine heterotrophic nanoflagellates (HNANs) are important grazers of picoplankton, yet knowledge on how prey type and temperature may affect HNAN feeding ecology remains limited. The relationship of temperature with growth rate, ingestion rate and gross growth efficiency was investigated for a HNAN feeding on either heterotrophic bacteria or the picoeukaryote Ostreococcus lucimarinus at 10°C, 15°C and 25°C, seasonal average temperatures typical in temperate North Carolina waters from which the organism originated. We found that the HNAN yielded similar growth (d−1) across the varying temperature regimes independent of diet, while gross growth efficiency was linked to differences in prey type. The HNAN ingestion rate (pg C HNAN−1 d−1) were strongly impacted by temperature, prey type and prey C concentrations with an interactive effect between temperature and prey type. Our study provides insight into individual picoplankton-HNAN trophic interactions in relation to varied temperature and prey environments and is meant to contribute to a better understanding of species-specific microbial dynamics which remain insufficiently detailed.
